## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- The sources found do not support this break's listed tide preference.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best wind direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> All 5 readable current sources were re-read (the WSL post read over https) and 2 new ones added: hawaii.surf and Caldwell & Aucan 2007 (JCR abstract). WIND (previously only 1 support) now has 3 readable publishers: Surf-Forecast ESE, hawaii.surf SE-S and WannaSurf S, all within 45 deg of 135. SWELL DIRECTION: NW from Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf and hawaii.surf (300-320, range 285-335). WSL shows the size is sensitive to swell direction. SIZE CONFLICT on the minimum: hawaii.surf says the bay doesn't break properly below 15 ft Hawaiian (30 ft faces), and the Eddie needs 30-40 ft faces (Wikipedia) or 40 ft (WSL). WannaSurf's text calls 15 ft a small day, while its template field says 3-5 ft (probably Pinballs and the shorebreak). The profile's 15 ft face minimum may be low for the main bay. Caldwell & Aucan show face height is about 2x the Hawaii scale. PERIOD: first numeric support is hawaii.surf (16+ s), consistent with 14/18. TIDE CONFLICT: hawaii.surf says mid-high is optimal (all workable) and Surfertoday (403) says medium tide, while the profile says all. No readable source says tide does not matter. SEASON: Wikipedia winter, hawaii.surf Nov-Mar (peak Dec-Feb), Caldwell & Aucan fall-spring (region-wide). Not readable (403): Surfertoday, GoHawaii (now magazine), SURFER. No measured bathymetry found. The Pacific Science erosion paper is not about surf.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | face: 30 ft; hawaiian: 15 ft [S7] · 15 ft; note: called a small day; scale: not stated [S5] · 3–5 ft (1–1.5 m); note: template field [S5] (Hawaiian scale and face as stated by hawaii.surf; otherwise not stated) | conflicting | S5, S7 | `wave_height_min_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | a large swell (no number) | documented | S7 | no separate setting; working range 15–45 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 40 ft or more; wannasurf template: 16 ft (5 m) or more (scale not stated) | documented | S4, S5, S6 | `wave_height_max_ft` 45 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: hawaii.surf says the bay doesn't break properly below 15 ft Hawaiian scale, which it equates with 30-foot faces, and WannaSurf's text calls 15 ft a small day, while WannaSurf's own template field says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft (the evidence file suggests this reflects Pinballs and the shorebreak).
  - S7 (hawaii.surf): “Minimum: 15 feet Hawaiian scale (30-foot faces) - Below this, the bay doesn't break properly”
  - S5 (WannaSurf): “Gets crowded when small (15ft !!)”
  - S5 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
- **Ideal range**: hawaii.surf describes the ideal as a large, long-period northwest groundswell; no excerpt gives an ideal size in numbers.
  - S7 (hawaii.surf): “A large, long-period northwest groundswell (16+ second intervals)”
- **Maximum suitable**: SURFER (search summary) says the Eddie Aikau contest runs only with 40-foot waves at Waimea, GoHawaii (search summary) that swells pound the bay with 30-foot waves, and WannaSurf's template that it holds 5 m / 16 ft and over; none gives a closed maximum or states the scale, and hawaii.surf's 25+ ft Hawaiian maximum is in the claim text, not its excerpt.
  - S6 (SURFER): “The Eddie Aikau contest runs only with 40-foot waves at Waimea Bay.”
  - S4 (GoHawaii.com (Hawaii tourism site)): “One says the ocean swells rising above the North Shore pound the Bay with 30-foot waves.”
  - S5 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: hawaii.surf says the bay doesn't break properly below 15 ft Hawaiian scale, which it equates with 30-foot faces, and WannaSurf's text calls 15 ft a small day, while WannaSurf's own template field says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft (the evidence file suggests this reflects Pinballs and the shorebreak).
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says offshore winds blow from the east-southeast, hawaii.surf gives a light offshore from southeast to south as ideal, and WannaSurf lists south as the good wind direction.
- **Geography · break type**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break with a right-breaking reef, while WannaSurf classes it as a point break over reef and sand and Wikipedia says the giant waves break off the northern point; WannaSurf also splits it into Waimea itself, Pinballs and the shorebreak.
